facts.statement: The genus Leptocleidus was first described by Andrews in 1922.
Leptocleidus was a small plesiosaur that grew to a maximum length of 3 meters.
facts.quote: It was comparatively small in size, measuring only up to 3 m in length.

facts.statement: The species L. capensis lived during the upper Valanginian age in the Cape Province of South Africa.
facts.quote: L. capensis is known from the Sundays River Formation (upper Valanginian age), Cape Province, South Africa.

facts.statement: L. clemai inhabited the Carnarvon Basin in Western Australia during the Hauterivian-Barremian ages.
facts.quote: L. clemai from the Birdrong Sandstone, found near Kalbarri in the Carnarvon Basin (Hauterivian-Barremian age) Western Australia.

facts.statement: L. superstes is known from the Upper Weald Clay in Sussex, England, dating to the Barremian age.
facts.quote: L. superstes is known from the Upper Weald Clay (Barremian age), Sussex, England.

facts.statement: Leptocleidus had a triangular skull featuring a crest extending from the nose tip to the nasal region.
facts.quote: The Leptocleidus triangle-shaped skull had a crest running from a ridge on the end of the nose to the nasal region.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Leptocleidus moved into freshwater systems to escape larger plesiosaurs and pliosaurs.
facts.quote: This led Arthur Richard Ivor Cruickshank to infer that this movement to fresh water was an attempt to flee larger plesiosaurs and pliosaurs.

facts.statement: Leptocleidus belongs to the family Leptocleididae.
Leptocleidus is classified within the order Plesiosauria.
Leptocleidus lived during the Cretaceous period in what is now England, Australia, and South Africa.
facts.quote: que vivieron en el Cretácico, en lo que hoy es Inglaterra, Australia y Sudáfrica.

facts.statement: The species L. superstes was the smallest, measuring approximately 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Leptocleidus superstes era casi un 50% más pequeño (1.5 metros) por lo que era la especie más pequeña.

facts.statement: Leptocleidus lived between 143.1 and 100.5 million years ago, from the Berriasian to the Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Albian (143.1 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Leptocleidus is L. superstes.
